answer: I'd like to talk about the time I taught my mother to use a smartphone, which was more of a challenge than I expected. A time I taught something to someone was when I helped her learn the basics about two years ago, because she had always found smartphones intimidating. She was keen to stay in touch with my elder sister in Dhaka and see her grandchildren more often, but felt hopelessly lost with the technology. I decided to teach her step by step, and I quickly realised how much [[patience]] it required. I had to slow right down and explain things I [[take for granted]], like swiping, typing a message or finding the camera. I wrote the steps in Bengali on a small card, which she kept beside her phone for months. There were moments of frustration on both sides, but she kept pressing the wrong buttons and then apologising, which made us both laugh. We persevered, usually with a cup of tea in the evenings. What made it so [[rewarding]] was watching her confidence grow, until she could video-call her grandchildren all by herself. Her delight was genuinely [[touching]], and it made every patient hour worthwhile. Honestly, the experience taught me as much as it taught her; it made me far more [[empathetic]] towards people who struggle with technology. It reminded me that teaching is really about seeing things through someone else's eyes. Seeing how much it improved her daily life was deeply satisfying. Now she sends me more messages than anyone else I know.

followUps.q: Do you enjoy teaching people things?
followUps.answer: I do, as long as the person is keen to learn. In my job I explain application processes to students every day, so I suppose teaching has become a natural part of my life.

followUps.q: What else would you like to teach your mother?
followUps.answer: Maybe online banking, so she doesn't have to queue at the bank. She is a little nervous about using money on her phone, though, so I will take it very slowly.

note: Persona fix: 'relatives abroad' became the elder sister in Dhaka and her children; added the Bengali instruction card; marked 'take for granted'.
